name: An SSH key bound to its projects is refused every other project
aliases: confine a coordinator to a project
summary: An SSH key can be bound to projects. ssh_forced_command.py takes --project NAME (repeatable) from its own arguments, which are the authorized_keys line and never the connection, and starts the endpoint with --key-project NAME for each; endpoint.execute then refuses, before anything else, every request whose project is not one of them, for every action (raw bd, session register, reviews, the merge slot, lifecycle facts, views), with ValueError Unknown/uninitialized project: the answer for a project that does not exist. The three web-only actions answer that they are for the web service. A line with no --project behaves as before. admin.py authorized-keys --project prints the bound contributor line (only that line; each name must be a project of the runtime). admin.py authorized-keys-list reads authorized_keys and says for each line whether it is unrestricted, confined, bound (with its projects), another command or unreadable, and flags a line that points at a kit other than the installed one. The key still names its own actor.
